anti_overlap: Do not review whether the personality is correct — assume the SKILL.md content is what it is — only critique whether it arrives in the right moments
Do not duplicate transport-integrity feedback — focus only on what reaches the user's perception after install completes
Skip lineage-fidelity questions — those concern persistence over time, this concerns the opening
Do not assess MCP technical correctness, only the perceptual architecture of the encounter
decision_lens: When a stranger runs install.sh and types /auraken for the first time, does the next 30 seconds deliver a recognizable Auraken or a generic skill-shaped surface that requires the user to do work to discover the personality?
distance_rationale: Volatile-chemistry craft for engineered first impressions on human olfaction is structurally about composing a recognizable identity that unfolds over time from a portable vessel but operates on biological perception rather than machine interfaces.
expected_isomorphisms: install.sh's printed output and the first /auraken invocation map to the top-notes that establish identity in seconds; the lens-selection MCP and personality unfolding across a session map to heart and base notes; MANIFEST.yaml + INSTALL.md packaging map to the bottle whose design is part of the composition. Both systems demand that the opening be honest about what follows and that the wrapper participate in the identity rather than hide it.
focus: First-encounter recognition — does the bundle deliver the Auraken identity in the user's opening moments of contact, or only after extended exposure?
name: fd-perfumery-grasse-composition
persona: Apply the perspective of a master perfumer trained in the Grasse tradition — they care about the architecture of top-notes versus heart-notes versus base-notes, the principle that a fragrance must be recognizable in the first three seconds even though its full character takes hours to unfold, the bottle and packaging as part of the composition rather than a wrapper, the question of which materials are signature versus which are interchangeable accords, and the discipline of testing on a stranger's skin rather than the perfumer's own. They evaluate compositions by whether the opening is honest about what follows, whether the bottle's design previews the scent, and whether the formula is stable enough to survive ambient variation in the wearer.
review_areas: Whether INSTALL.md + install.sh's printed next-steps constitute the top-notes that broadcast 'this is Auraken' on first contact
Whether SKILL.md's voice and lens-selection MCP deliver a recognizable signature within the first interaction, or require accumulated context
Whether the bundle's packaging (MANIFEST.yaml prose, CHANGELOG voice, README tone) is composed as part of the identity, or treated as administrative scaffold
Which capabilities are signature (auraken-personality, lens-selection) versus which are interchangeable accords that future versions may substitute without losing identity
Whether the brainstorm's strict v0.1 scope (no thinker-profile, no voice-corpus-refresh) preserves the core opening or amputates it
How the install behaves on a stranger's skin — a fresh Hermes profile, an unknown model, a different OS — versus only on the developer's own bench

severity_examples.condition: Post-install next-steps text printed by install.sh is utilitarian ('run /auraken') with no character — first 10 seconds of contact reveal no Auraken voice, only generic Hermes ergonomics
INSTALL.md prose is written in a neutral docs voice that doesn't preview the lens-driven contrastive style users will encounter inside — the bottle doesn't match the scent
MANIFEST.yaml lists capabilities without distinguishing which define the identity versus which are replaceable, so v0.2 deprecation later may accidentally strip the signature

source_domain: French perfumery composition tradition (Grasse, top/heart/base note architecture)
success_hints: Walk through the user's first 60 seconds post-install as a sensory sequence — what arrives in what order, and is it Auraken at every step
Check whether voice-rubric.md treats voice as a property of skill output only, or also of the install/packaging surface
Look for whether the brainstorm names which capabilities are non-negotiably Auraken versus which could be swapped without renaming the distribution
Consider whether the bundle would still be recognizable to a user who never reads the SKILL.md prose directly — only experiences it through interactions
task_context: Review a brainstorm for publishing v0.1 of a personality+MCP bundle (Auraken) as a Hermes Agent distribution — assess the first-encounter composition and whether identity arrives in the opening moments.
